synopsis: EN 14363:2016+A2:2022 governs acceptance of railway vehicle running behavior, with informative Annex T addressing simulation of on-track tests and Annex U extending acceptance to vehicles of the same basic design [f15362, f14674]. It is the only standard identified in the booklet that formally allows validated simulation to extend acceptance to new conditions and modified vehicles; running tests validate the model, and physical running tests remain required for the reference vehicle [f14672, f14675, f8136]. Validation uses at least 24 simulation-versus-measurement comparisons from at least 12 track sections, applying limits to the whole set of deviations; the associated DynoTRAIN study used more than 1,000 comparisons during the 2014–2022 case [f15363, f15364, f7854, f7855]. The booklet identifies this framework as the strongest family-transfer and test-reduction precedent for off-road automatic braking, but qualifies its relevance because rail physics is far more deterministic than perception and the framework has no formal risk scaling [f8137, f8138, f8132]. No percentage of physical tests removed across actual rail certifications was published, and no documented accident in which an EN 14363-validated simulation itself created false confidence was found [f7856, f7990].
